From 591f762b2750c628df9412d1c795b56e83a34b3e Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Yixian Liu <liuyixian@huawei.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2021 15:12:30 +0800
Subject: [PATCH] RDMA/hns: Remove the condition of light load for posting DWQE

Even in the case of heavy load, direct WQE can still be posted. The
hardware will decide whether to drop the DWQE or not. Thus, the limit
needs to be removed.

Fixes: 01584a5edcc4 ("RDMA/hns: Add support of direct wqe")
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/1619593950-29414-1-git-send-email-liweihang@huawei.com
Signed-off-by: Yixian Liu <liuyixian@huawei.com>
Signed-off-by: Weihang Li <liweihang@huawei.com>
Signed-off-by: Jason Gunthorpe <jgg@nvidia.com>

diff --git a/drivers/infiniband/hw/hns/hns_roce_hw_v2.c b/drivers/infiniband/hw/hns/hns_roce_hw_v2.c
index 7652dafe32ec..49bb4f51466c 100644
--- a/drivers/infiniband/hw/hns/hns_roce_hw_v2.c
+++ b/drivers/infiniband/hw/hns/hns_roce_hw_v2.c
@@ -791,8 +791,7 @@ static int hns_roce_v2_post_send(struct ib_qp *ibqp,
 		qp->sq.head += nreq;
 		qp->next_sge = sge_idx;
 
-		if (nreq == 1 && qp->sq.head == qp->sq.tail + 1 &&
-		    (qp->en_flags & HNS_ROCE_QP_CAP_DIRECT_WQE))
+		if (nreq == 1 && (qp->en_flags & HNS_ROCE_QP_CAP_DIRECT_WQE))
 			write_dwqe(hr_dev, qp, wqe);
 		else
 			update_sq_db(hr_dev, qp);
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `drivers/infiniband/hw/hns/hns_roce_hw_v2.c`**
   - The condition that checks for "light load" (specifically, `qp->sq.head == qp->sq.tail + 1`) has been removed from the `if` statement that determines whether to write a direct WQE (Work Queue Element).
   - The modified condition now only checks if `nreq == 1` and if the `qp->en_flags` indicates support for direct WQE (`HNS_ROCE_QP_CAP_DIRECT_WQE`).

### Relationships Between Modifications

- The change simplifies the logic for posting direct WQEs by allowing them to be posted regardless of the queue's load state. This means that even under heavy load, the hardware will still have the opportunity to process direct WQEs, as it will decide whether to drop them based on its own internal mechanisms. The removal of the light load condition aligns the behavior with the hardware's capabilities, ensuring that the posting of direct WQEs is not unnecessarily restricted.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
if (nreq == 1 && qp->sq.head == qp->sq.tail + 1 &&
    (qp->en_flags & HNS_ROCE_QP_CAP_DIRECT_WQE))
```
```c
if (nreq == 1 && qp->sq.head == qp->sq.tail + 1)
```
Reason:
The original condition checks if the queue is in a "light load" state (i.e., `qp->sq.head == qp->sq.tail + 1`) before allowing a direct WQE to be posted. This unnecessarily restricts the posting of direct WQEs to only when the queue is not heavily loaded, which contradicts the hardware's capability to handle WQEs under heavy load.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
if (nreq == 1 && (qp->en_flags & HNS_ROCE_QP_CAP_DIRECT_WQE))
```
Reason:
The patch removes the condition that checks for the queue's load state, allowing direct WQEs to be posted regardless of whether the queue is under heavy load. This aligns the software logic with the hardware's ability to manage WQEs, enabling more efficient handling of requests.
